Simulate age-year-space covariance using SPDE approach

Source: R/sim_dist_spde.R
sim_ays_covar_spde.Rd

sim_ays_covar_spde(
  sd = 2.8,
  range = 300,
  model = "spde",
  phi_age = 0.5,
  phi_year = 0.9,
  group_ages = 5:20,
  group_years = NULL,
  mesh,
  barrier.triangles
)

Arguments

sd

Variance of the process (can be age-specific).

range

Decorrelation range.

model

Either "barrier" or "spde"; determines how the precision matrix Q is generated.

phi_age

Autocorrelation through ages. Can be a single value or a vector the same length as ages.

phi_year

Autocorrelation through years. Can be a single value or a vector the same length as years.

group_ages

Ages to group together for shared space-age-year variance.

group_years

Years to group together for shared space-age-year variance.

mesh

An fm_mesh_2d or legacy inla.mesh object used to generate the precision matrix. Stored legacy meshes, including the meshes inside survey_mesh and survey_lite_mesh, are converted automatically when fmesher is available. Conversion preserves vertices and triangle indices.

barrier.triangles

The set of mesh triangles that define the barrier (used only in the barrier model).

Value

A function that can be passed to sim_distribution() as the ays_covar argument.

Details

Returns a function for use inside sim_distribution() to generate the error term.

For a bundled mesh, supply survey_mesh$mesh (or survey_lite_mesh$mesh). With model = "barrier", also supply its matching barrier_tri component as barrier.triangles. Legacy conversion updates the object representation, not the triangulation or the numbering used by these barrier indices. The original supplied mesh and bundled data are not modified.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("INLA")) {

  # Make a grid
  my_grid <- make_grid(res = c(10, 10))

  # Make a mesh based on the grid
  my_mesh <- make_mesh(my_grid)

  # Simulate and plot
  sim <- sim_abundance(ages = 1:10, years = 1:10) |>
    sim_distribution(
      grid = my_grid,
      ays_covar = sim_ays_covar_spde(
        phi_age = 0.8,
        phi_year = 0.1,
        model = "spde",
        mesh = my_mesh
      ),
      depth_par = sim_parabola(mu = 200, sigma = 50)
    )

  plot_distribution(sim, ages = 1:5, years = 1:5, type = "heatmap")
}


# }
